extracted.intended_audience: European Commission services preparing initiatives and proposals; policymakers; stakeholders (citizens, businesses, civil society) participating in EU consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Official European Commission guidance describing principles, instruments and procedural requirements for designing, evaluating and simplifying EU laws and for engaging stakeholders across the policy lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simpler, lighter, and faster EU regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: EU regulation should be simpler, lighter and faster; the Commission strives to simplify and lighten the administrative burden of EU regulations to ensure they are proportionate, stable, coherent, and technology neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching objective underpins the better regulation agenda and motivates simplification and implementation priorities; guidance and toolbox provide concrete support to Commission services preparing initiatives or managing existing legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based policies and laws
rubrics_metrics.description: EU actions must be informed by the best available evidence and designed to achieve desired impact to bring benefits for EU society, economy and environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better regulation aims to deliver evidence-based policies and laws that achieve their objectives in the most efficient way; use evaluations, fitness checks and impact assessments to gather and apply evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor-made to needs of citizens, businesses and civil society
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and laws should be designed to be tailormade to the needs of EU citizens, businesses and civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder input across the lifecycle (consultations, implementation dialogues, reality checks, calls for evidence) is used to ensure initiatives are adapted to real-world needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate-first principle (evaluations and fitness checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation precedes work on the revision of an existing policy or law and provides evidence to the problem definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission evaluations and fitness checks analyse performance of existing policies/programmes/legislation, assessing effectiveness, relevance, coherence and EU added value; they inform preparation of reviews or new initiatives and feed into stress-testing the acquis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessments examine whether there is a need for EU action, analyse the possible impacts of available solutions and guide Commission choice and preparation of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This analysis is carried out during the preparation phase, before finalising a proposal for a new or revised law; impact assessments are subject to quality control (e.g., Regulatory Scrutiny Board review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic foresight
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic foresight is used as a tool to create future-proof and coherent policies by exploring different possible futures and associated opportunities and challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foresight helps policymakers act in the present to shape the future and should be integrated alongside evaluations and impact assessments to ensure policies are resilient to future challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplification and REFIT burden-reduction targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission aims to make EU laws simpler and reduce unnecessary regulatory costs while achieving intended objectives; REFIT targets a reduction of existing administrative burdens by at least 25% and by 35% for SMEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stress-testing the EU acquis through evaluations and fitness checks generates simplification proposals; the 'one in, one out' approach ensures burdens introduced are offset by removing equivalent burdens in the same policy area.

rubrics_metrics.name: One in, one out approach
rubrics_metrics.description: All burdens introduced by Commission initiatives are considered and administrative burdens are offset by removing burdens of equivalent value in the same policy area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational rule supports the REFIT objective of reducing overall administrative burden and is part of the Commission's simplification strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME and competitiveness check
rubrics_metrics.description: A new SME and competitiveness check is applied to better capture these dimensions in impact assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This check complements impact assessments to ensure competitiveness and SME impacts are considered; the Commission publishes a yearly overview of simplification and burden-reduction efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control: Regulatory Scrutiny Board review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Scrutiny Board (independent body of Commission officials and external experts) reviews impact assessments and selected evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board provides independent scrutiny and publishes annual reports on its activity to ensure quality and consistency of impact assessments and selected evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiarity principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In line with subsidiarity, the Commission aims to act only where necessary and where it delivers clear benefits over measures taken at national, regional or local levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subsidiarity grid is attached to all politically sensitive and important initiatives accompanied by an impact assessment to document this consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportionality focuses on minimising the financial and administrative impact of proposed legislation to ensure regulatory actions do not exceed what is necessary to achieve objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any impact must be minimised and proportionate to the policy objectives; policies should be delivered in the simplest and least costly way, avoiding unnecessary red tape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement: central principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Consulting stakeholders is central — the Commission offers opportunities for feedback online over the entire lifecycle of a policy to collect evidence and ensure transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should be centralised, multilingual, transparent and easy to use; contributions feed into the decision-making process and help deliver higher-quality, more robust initiatives and evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for evidence (timing and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for evidence (for impact assessments, evaluations and fitness checks) are open for a period of 4 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for evidence solicit views, practical experience, evidence and data from stakeholders to inform problem definition and option appraisal during preparation of IAs and evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public consultation (timing and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public consultations for legislative acts are open for a period of 12 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public consultations collect stakeholder views and evidence on proposed legislative acts and are a core mechanism for transparency and input into policy proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual access and e-translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Both calls for evidence and public consultations are in principle available in all official EU languages; Europeans can contribute in any of the 24 official EU languages and receive informal e-translation of feedback/comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures accessibility and inclusiveness of stakeholder engagement across Member States and language groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback on draft legislative and delegated/implementing acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens can share feedback on proposals of legal acts or delegated and implementing acts; the Commission analyses and sums up feedback and contributions received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries of feedback allow Europeans to see how their input contributes to preparation of initiatives; feedback on draft legislative acts is shared with co-legislators (European Parliament and Council).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation dialogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Member of the European Commission will organise at least two implementation dialogues with stakeholders each year to align implementation of EU law with realities on the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dialogues provide an open platform to identify obstacles to proper implementation; outcomes feed into stress-testing of legislation and the design of simplification proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reality checks with practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Reality checks reach out to practitioners in companies to understand experience on the ground and the impact of EU law on their activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical exchanges identify practical issues, hurdles or positive experiences related to implementation and national transposition; outcomes feed into evaluations, fitness checks and simplification design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interinstitutional partnership and political dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving EU law-making is a shared responsibility of the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission; the Commission will relaunch political dialogue to discuss ideas and assess amendment impacts jointly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working more closely together allows all parties to assess impacts of their amendments consistently and to fulfil commitments under the interinstitutional agreement on better law‑making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation by Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: Member States must fully implement EU rules in a timely fashion and ensure they are correctly applied and enforced to deliver intended benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor implementation creates costs and legal insecurity for people and businesses; effective enforcement and correct transposition are essential for delivering EU objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: International regulatory cooperation and external context
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's better regulation policy requires taking account of the international context, including international treaties and agreements, geopolitical impacts, WTO notification and mainstreaming UN Sustainable Development Goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact assessments and evaluations should address international obligations and impacts; cooperation and consideration of global standards inform policy development and external consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and public reporting of engagement and simplification progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission monitors and reports on consultation activity and simplification efforts (e.g., portal metrics and yearly overviews of burden-reduction progress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public figures (visits, number of consultations, contributions, feedback published) and yearly overviews on simplification help show progress and accountability toward better regulation objectives.
